### 1. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-123`  (both, easy, 40 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Tree-planting activities are popular with schools, offices and companies, but foresters warn that planting is only the first step. Photos of volunteers holding seedlings are easy to take, but the real test comes months later, after the volunteers have gone home. Many seedlings die within a year because no one waters them or clears the weeds that grow around them. In some cases, the wrong species are planted, such as trees that cannot survive the dry season of a given area. A provincial environment office now asks groups that plan a tree-planting activity to commit to caring for the seedlings for at least three years. Groups must choose native species suited to the site and must report how many seedlings survive each year. Some companies complained that the rule made tree planting harder to organize. The office replied that a smaller number of surviving trees is worth more than a large number of dead seedlings. Since the rule began, survival rates at monitored sites have improved greatly.

As used in the passage, the word "commit" most nearly means

- (A) refuse
- (B) do something wrong
- (C) promise
- (D) report

### 2. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-131`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

In a remote island barangay in Palawan, mobile phone signals are weak and internet access is unreliable. News from the town center once reached residents days late, usually by word of mouth from boatmen. To keep residents informed, the barangay council started a small community radio station run by volunteers. Each morning, the station reads weather updates, fishing advisories and announcements from the barangay hall. On weekends, it airs a program in which the midwife answers health questions sent in by listeners on paper slips. During a recent storm, the station stayed on air with a generator and told families when it was safe to return home from the evacuation center. Residents say they trust the station because they know the volunteers personally. The council now wants to train young residents to run the station, since several of the original volunteers are getting older. A neighboring barangay has also asked for help in starting its own station.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) The midwife's health program for mothers in the barangay
- (B) A volunteer radio station that keeps an isolated barangay informed
- (C) How volunteers can build a generator for a radio station
- (D) Weak phone signals in remote parts of the Philippines

### 5. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-141`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

A consumer group surveyed small stores in a city and found that many did not display prices on their goods. The survey covered sari-sari stores, small hardware stores and food stalls near public schools. Shoppers had to ask, and some said they received different prices on different days. Under consumer protection rules, goods offered for sale should carry a clear price tag. The city's trade office began a campaign that combined reminders and inspections. Inspectors first visited stores to explain the rule and gave out free price tag sheets. A month later, they returned to check. Stores that still had no tags received a written warning, and only those that ignored the warning were fined. The trade office reports that most stores complied after the first visit. Store owners said that tags actually saved them time, since they no longer had to answer the same price question many times a day.

According to the passage, what happened to stores that ignored the written warning?

- (A) They were fined
- (B) They were given another month
- (C) They were closed
- (D) They received free price tags

### 8. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-151`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Children from a hillside barangay in Rizal used to cross a shallow river on stepping stones to reach their school. The crossing took only a few minutes in the dry months, and older pupils often helped the younger ones. During heavy rain, the river rose quickly, and teachers often sent pupils home early to avoid danger. Parents had asked for a bridge for years, but the cost of a concrete bridge was far beyond the barangay's budget. Last year, a group of engineering students from a state university offered a cheaper design: a hanging footbridge made of steel cables and wooden planks. Residents provided the labor, and the municipality paid for the materials. The bridge took four months to finish. It is too narrow for vehicles, but it lets children cross safely in any weather. Teachers say that early dismissals because of rain have almost stopped. The engineering students now check the cables twice a year as part of their course.

Which title best fits the passage?

- (A) Why Rivers Rise After Rain
- (B) Building Concrete Bridges
- (C) A Low-Cost Bridge That Keeps Pupils Safe
- (D) Engineering Courses in Rizal

### 11. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-161`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Pharmacists in a provincial hospital noticed that many patients, especially older ones, took their medicines at the wrong times. Some took two doses at once, while others skipped doses because they were unsure of the schedule. Labels with small printed instructions were often hard to read, and some patients could not read English well. The pharmacy began using picture labels. A sun means the medicine is taken in the morning, a plate means it is taken with a meal, and a moon means it is taken at night. Pharmacists also explain the pictures to the patient and a family member before the patient goes home. A follow-up check found that patients with picture labels made fewer mistakes than those with printed labels only. The pharmacy still prints the written instructions, since nurses and other pharmacists need the exact details. The head pharmacist says the pictures do not replace explanation; they help patients remember it.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) How picture labels helped patients take medicines correctly
- (B) Why older patients dislike going to hospitals
- (C) Why medicine labels in English should be banned
- (D) How nurses read and check doctors' prescriptions

### 14. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-171`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

When a city in Metro Manila painted protected bike lanes on two main roads, critics predicted that the lanes would stay empty while cars sat in worse traffic. Supporters replied that people would ride if they felt safe from cars, and the city decided to test the idea. A year later, counts by the city's transport office show a mixed picture. On one road, which connects a residential area to a train station, the number of cyclists has more than tripled, and many are workers riding to the station. On the other road, which passes through a business district with few homes nearby, the lanes are used far less. Car traffic on both roads is about the same as before. The office concludes that bike lanes work best when they link places where people live to places they need to go. It now plans to extend the lanes from the busy road into nearby neighborhoods rather than paint new lanes in the business district.

What is the main idea of the passage?

- (A) Bike lanes always reduce car traffic
- (B) Train stations need more parking
- (C) Critics were right that the lanes would stay empty
- (D) Bike lanes are used most when they connect homes to destinations

### 17. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC-181`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

A regional office noticed that clients often had to fill out the same personal details on three or four separate forms. A single request, such as a certificate, could take a client half an hour of writing before reaching the counter. Name, address and birth date were written again and again, and errors crept in when clients grew tired or rushed. A team of employees reviewed every form the office used and found that many fields could be combined. They designed a single intake sheet that collects the basic details once; the other forms now ask only for information specific to each request. The team tested the new sheet with clients for two weeks before adopting it. Clients took less time at the counter, and staff found fewer mismatched entries. The team also removed two forms that were no longer required by any rule. The regional director has asked other offices in the region to review their own forms in the same way.

According to the passage, what does the single intake sheet do?

- (A) It is filled out by staff only
- (B) It replaces every other form completely
- (C) It collects the basic personal details once
- (D) It is used only for new employees

### 20. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC2-011`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

In a farming town in Nueva Ecija, an old storeroom behind the municipal hall now holds hundreds of glass jars of seeds. Each jar is labeled with the name of a rice, corn or vegetable variety, the farm it came from and the year it was harvested. The collection began after a typhoon flooded the lowland fields and ruined the seed that many families had saved for the next planting. Farmers who wanted to replant had to buy commercial seed, which was costly and did not always suit the local soil. A retired agriculturist suggested that the town keep a shared reserve. Farmers now deposit a small part of each harvest and may borrow seed when they need it, returning twice the amount after their next harvest. The arrangement is not free of problems. Seeds lose their ability to sprout if they are stored too long or kept in damp jars, so volunteers test a sample from each jar every year. Even so, the storeroom has already supplied seed to forty households after a second flood.

What is the passage mainly about?

- (A) A shared seed reserve that helps farmers replant after disasters
- (B) Why commercial seed is better than saved seed
- (C) How typhoons damage lowland rice fields
- (D) The history of farming in the Philippines

### 24. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC2-021`  (both, easy, 45 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

Every Friday, a street in a Cagayan de Oro barangay closes to traffic and fills with food stalls. The night market began as a way to help small vendors, but within a year residents were complaining about the noise, the smoke from grills and the trash left behind until morning. Instead of closing the market, the barangay council met with vendors and residents together. They agreed on a short list of rules. Grills must sit at the downwind end of the street, music must stop at ten, and every vendor must clean the space in front of the stall before leaving. A vendor who breaks a rule twice loses the stall for a month. The rules were posted on a board at both entrances so that customers, too, would know what to expect. Complaints fell sharply in the following months. The council credits the change less to the penalties than to the meeting itself, where residents and vendors heard each other's concerns for the first time and wrote rules that both groups considered fair.

According to the passage, what happens to a vendor who breaks a rule twice?

- (A) The vendor pays a fine to the barangay
- (B) The vendor is banned from the market for good
- (C) The vendor loses the stall for a month
- (D) The vendor must move to the downwind end

### 26. `CIVIO-D1022-VEN-RC2-031`  (both, medium, 60 s)

Read the passage, then answer the question.

When food prices rose sharply one year, a public elementary school in Leyte turned a muddy corner of its grounds into a vegetable garden. Pupils in the upper grades were assigned small plots, and each class kept a notebook recording what was planted, how often it was watered and how much was harvested. Teachers used the notebooks in their lessons. In mathematics, pupils compared the yields of different plots; in science, they tested whether plots with compost grew faster than plots without it. The harvest went to the school's feeding program for pupils who were underweight. At first some parents objected, saying their children were sent to school to study, not to farm. Their view changed when they saw the notebooks at a parents' meeting and realized that the garden was part of the lessons rather than a distraction from them. Several parents later donated seedlings and tools. The principal admits that the garden does not feed every child who needs help, but she says it has taught pupils that what they learn in class can be used outside it.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

- (A) A school garden became both a food source and a way to teach regular lessons
- (B) Food prices in Leyte rose so sharply one year that families went hungry
- (C) Pupils with compost plots always harvest more than pupils without compost
